versions.changelog: wp; wp; Safety rule 1, the frontmatter security note and the 1; wp-credentials; Fail-closed route policy: only creating a draft post/page or a new category/tag is free; other content writes ; wp-upload; The loader ignores WP_ALLOW_* lines in env files, with a warning; SKILL
Remove mandatory GitHub CTA from SEO guidance; outbound links must be relevant and user-requested.
Canonical route authorization, validated .env, netrc cleanup trap, no curl -u.
Keep credentials off argv (netrc file), canonicalize REST routes before consent gates, HTTPS+allowlist+live-edit gates from 1.3.0.

Enforce advertised safety in code: HTTPS required, host allowlist always on, live PUT/PATCH gated, encoded force= blocked, upload env-file ownership/mode/symlink checks. No credential files in the zip.

Fixes the three findings that kept the DO_NOT_INSTALL banner. (1) JSON injection: media alt-text was interpolated into a JSON string, so any quote broke or altered the payload — now built with a real encoder. (2) WP_ENV_FILE is credentials input and is validated as trusted: absolute path, no symlink, owned by the caller, mode 0600, else refuse. (3) Adds a machine-readable permissions block declaring network, shell, env, file and credential scope.

Summary now states the enforced safety instead of claiming blanket draft-only: reads free, publish/live-edit/plugin-install refused without per-action opt-in (WP_ALLOW_PUBLISH / WP_ALLOW_ADMIN), host allowlist checked before any request leaves the machine.

Security and disclosure pass. Adds a Permissions, Data Flow & Consent section declaring every capability, what data is touched, where it is written and what leaves the machine. Documents the off-switch and requires explicit opt-in for privacy-affecting or destructive actions. Removes documentation claims the shipped code did not implement. No functionality removed.
Initial release — REST API wrapper with draft-only safety, SEO via Yoast, media uploads, plugin management.
